purpose: One unambiguous toll crossing, priced by hand from the published tariff and every company's program terms. Checks crossing detection, time of day pricing, and the toll decision end to end.
assumptions: Saturday 21 November 2026, depart 10:00 Eastern, return 18:00 Eastern the same day, so the rental is 1 day.
The only tolled facility is the George Washington Bridge, eastbound into New York. The Port Authority tolls only that direction, so the return leg is free.
The car reaches the bridge within minutes, before 11:00, which is the weekend off peak window. E-ZPass off peak is 14.79. Tolls by Mail is 23.30 at all hours.
Washington Heights is north of 60th Street, outside the congestion relief zone, so congestion is 0.
The toll is crossed on 1 day, so a fee charged per usage day is charged once.
Rental base rates are placeholders of 100.00 per company, not quotes. They only fix the rental line so it cannot vary.
Hertz, Dollar, Thrifty per crossing: 9.99 for the 1 usage day plus the toll at the plate rate 23.30, which is 33.29.
Avis and Budget per crossing: 6.95 for the 1 rental day, cap not reached, plus 23.30, which is 30.25.
Enterprise per crossing: 4.95 for the 1 usage day plus the toll at the E-ZPass rate 14.79, which is 19.74.
Unlimited, 1 day: Hertz 27.99, Avis and Budget 25.99, Dollar and Thrifty 21.49. Tolls included, no congestion to add.
The cheapest per company is therefore the unlimited plan, except Enterprise, which has no unlimited plan.
There is no overnight stay, so no hotel is priced. Per docs/API.md, hotelCents is 0 and provenance.hotelSource is null, and freshness.hotel reads UNAVAILABLE.

sources.source: PANYNJ tariff effective 4 January 2026, as recorded in data/seeds/SOURCES.md, Port Authority section
Company toll program terms, as recorded in data/seeds/SOURCES.md, rental company toll programs section

scope: Verifies the computation against published tariffs and program terms. It does not verify real market prices, so it is not evidence for SC1.
